'''Sir Jack Edward Baldwin''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|FRS}}<ref name=frs/> (8 August 1938<ref name=AAAS>{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter B|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterB.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|accessdate=9 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title = Birthdays | newspaper = [[The Guardian]] | pages = 39 | date = 8 Aug 2014}}</ref> – 5 January 2020<ref name = Oxford>{{cite web |title=Sir Jack Baldwin FRS (individual news story) |url=https://www.chem.ox.ac.uk/chemistry-news-item.aspx?ID=2761 |website=Department of Chemistry, University of Oxford |accessdate=9 January 2020 |archive-date=14 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114152627/https://www.chem.ox.ac.uk/chemistry-news-item.aspx?ID=2761 |url-status=dead }}</ref>) was a British [[chemist]]. He was a [[Waynflete Professorships|Waynflete Professor of Chemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]] (1978–2005)<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Moses |first1=John E. |last2=Adlington |first2=Robert M. |title=Sir Jack Baldwin, FRS: Biomimetic studies at Oxford |journal=Chemical Communications |date=2005 |issue=48 |pages=5945–5952 |doi=10.1039/B512961C |pmid=16333494 |accessdate=9 January 2020|url=https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlelanding/2005/cc/b512961c|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and head of the [[organic chemistry]] at Oxford.<ref>{{cite web |url =http://www.rsc.org/Publishing/Journals/cc/News/BaldwinInterview.asp |title =Interview with Baldw in Chem. Commun., 24 January 2006 |url-status =dead |archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20061011200312/http://www.rsc.org/Publishing/Journals/cc/News/BaldwinInterview.asp |archive-date =11 October 2006 }}</ref><ref>{{Scopus id }}</ref>

==Education ==
Baldwin was the second son of Frederick C N Baldwin and Olive F Headland. He was educated at Brighton Grammar School and [[Priory School, Lewes|Lewes County Grammar School]]. He attended [[Imperial College, London]] (BSc, DIC, PhD)<ref name="burke"/> and received his Ph.D. working under the direction of [[Derek Barton|Sir Derek H.R. Barton, FRS, Nobel Laureate]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Harwood |first1=Laurence |last2=Adlington |first2=Robert |title=Laudation for Professor Sir Jack Baldwin FRS |journal=Synlett |date=August 2008 |volume=2008 |issue=14 |pages=I–III |doi=10.1055/s-2008-1078258 |url=https://www.thieme-connect.com/products/ejournals/pdf/10.1055/s-2008-1078258.pdf |accessdate=10 January 2020|doi-access=free }}</ref> who described him as his best student.<ref name = Oxford/>

==Career and research ==
After four years on the staff at Imperial College, Baldwin moved to the United States: first to [[Pennsylvania State University]]  in 1967 and then to [[MIT]] in 1970,<ref>{{cite web|title=Jack E. Baldwin|website=Chemistry Tree|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=57597|access-date=26 April 2020}}</ref> where he published his most significant work — [[Baldwin's rules]] for ring closure reactions. It was also where Baldwin met his future wife, Christine Louise Franchi; they married in 1977. In 1978, he moved to [[Oxford]] to become head of the [[Dyson Perrins Laboratory]], where he upgraded its facilities and revolutionised the type of work done, while building links between Organic Chemistry and basic biological research. The laboratory formally closed in 2003, but his group moved to the new research facility, the [[Chemistry Research Laboratory, University of Oxford|Chemistry Research Laboratory]] on Mansfield Road.

One of Baldwin's passions was finding out how nature makes chemicals that researchers cannot. This led him to ‘biomimetic’ synthesis: using the principles of nature to improve the generation of biomolecules in the laboratory.<ref name = Ferry>{{cite journal|last=Ferry|first=Georgina|title=Obituary: Jack Baldwin (1938-2020)|journal=Nature|volume=578|page=212|date=13 February 2020|doi=10.1038/d41586-020-00357-1 |s2cid=211054600 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

The Baldwin group’s range of interests includes mechanisms of reactions; total synthesis of natural products such as trichoviridin, [[acromelic acid A]], [[hypoglycin A]] and [[lactacystin]];  and biomimetic synthesis of natural products such as (-)-xestospongin A. Baldwin published over 700 papers.<ref name = Oxford/>

Georgina Ferry's obituary of Baldwin<ref name = Ferry/> notes that "he had little time for the academic conventions of Oxford: he spoke his mind." and that "he enjoyed good food, fine wine, powerful motorbikes, fast cars and his dogs." Some of these aspects of his character are illustrated in a three-part documentary.<ref>See Parts I (first 1:50 min.) ''and'' III (all)  {{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QhzxlcVjJis |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/QhzxlcVjJis |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=The Cutting Edge|work=[[YouTube]]|date=16 December 2006 |access-date=30 April 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

===Some positions held===

Derived from Who's Who 2020.<ref name=who/>

*1963 Assistant Lecturer in Chemistry, Imperial College
*1966 Lecturer
*1967 Assistant Professor of Chemistry, Penn State
*1969 Associate Professor
*1969-70 Alfred P. Sloan Fellow
*1970 Associate Professor of Chemistry
*1972 [[John Frederic Daniell|Daniell]] Professor of Chemistry, King’s College, London
*1972-78 Professor of Chemistry, MIT

*1975 Corday Morgan Medal and Prize, [[Chemical Society]]<ref name=who>{{Who's Who | year= 2020 | title=Baldwin, Sir Jack (Edward)| id= U6289 | doi= 10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U6289}}</ref>
*1978 Elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name=frs>{{cite web |url =https://royalsociety.org/people/jack-baldwin-11026/ |title =Jack Baldwin FRS |website =royalsociety.org |author =Anon |location =London |publisher =[[Royal Society]] |year =1978 |url-status =dead |archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20151117132111/https://royalsociety.org/people/jack-baldwin-11026/ |archive-date =2015-11-17 }}</ref>
*1984 [[Paul Karrer Gold Medal]] at the [[University of Zurich]]<ref name=who/>
*1987 Hugo Müller Medal, Royal Society of Chemistry<ref name=who/>
*1987 [[Max Tishler]] Award, Harvard University<ref name=who/>
*1988 Dr Paul Jansen Prize for Creativity in Organic Synthesis, Belgium
*1993 [[Davy Medal]]<ref name="royalsocbiog" />
*1994 Elected a Foreign Honorary Member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name=AAAS />
*1997 Invested as a Knight Bachelor<ref name="burke"/>

*2002 [[Nakanishi Prize#Recipients|Nakanishi Prize]]
*2006 Paracelsus Prize<ref name="royalsocbiog">{{cite web |title=Jack Baldwin (Fellows Directory) |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/jack-baldwin-11026/ |website=The Royal Society |accessdate=9 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Paracelsus Prize|website=Swiss Chemical Society|url=https://scg.ch/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=89&Itemid=587&lang=en|access-date=26 April 2020|archive-date=7 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200807154854/https://scg.ch/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=89&Itemid=587&lang=en|url-status=dead}}</ref>
